newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper sets referendum on peace.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper sets referendum on peace.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper said on Monday his government would ask Colombians to endorse tentative government moves toward peace with leftist guerrillas in a referendum next October.
In his weekly television and radio address, Samper said the referendum would be held on the sidelines of gubernatorial and mayoral elections across Colombia on Oct. 26.
"Conditions permitting, we will invite all Colombians to pronounce themselves, in a sort of plebiscite, in favour of a mandate for peace and life," Samper said.

Samper called for unconditional peace talks with Colombia's Marxist-led rebels in a statement last Friday and said the government recognised them as a legitimate political force. But top rebel leaders shot down the proposal almost immediately, saying they had no interest in negotiating with an "illegitimate government."
Samper, who hands over power in August 1998, has been severely weakened since the early days of his administration by charges that he received drug money to help finance his 1994 campaign.
In his speech, Samper conceded that "peace is not just around the corner" and that the war, which he said is costing Colombia nearly $4 billion a year, is unlikely to end before he leaves office.

But he said his government was seriously interested in getting a peace process on track, however slowly it moves forward at the start, and urged rebels to make certain "gestures" indicating they too were interested in pacifying a country torn by more than three decades of politcial bloodshed.

Among other gestures, he urged guerrillas to release 60 soldiers held hostage since an attack on a military base eight months ago and to free all of kidnap victims they are currently holding across Colombia.
